title_original: Ava DuVernay to Receive London Critics’ Circle’s Inaugural Female Trailblazer Award
excerpt_original: The London Critics’ Circle is adding another special award to its 2027 film awards ceremony and has tapped Ava DuVernay as the first recipient. The Laura Mulvey Female Trailblazer Award — named after renowned film theorist and filmmaker (and Critics’ Circle member) Laura Mulvey…

blocks.text: The London Critics’ Circle is adding another special award to its 2027 film awards ceremony and has tapped Ava DuVernay as the first recipient.

The Laura Mulvey Female Trailblazer Award — named after renowned film theorist and filmmaker (and Critics’ Circle member) Laura Mulvey — will, according to the Circle, recognize the “most influential women in film, who are working to break the glass ceiling, change the cultural conversation and be an example of what is possible for future generations.”

blocks.text: DuVernay, the groundbreaking director behind “Selma,” “13th” and “Origin” and a Emmy, BAFTA, Sundance and Peabody winner, is also the driving force behind arts and social impact collective ARRAY. Her latest documentary “14th” — exploring the history and ongoing fight around the U.S. Constitution’s 14th amendment — is getting a limited theatrical run in the U.S. and U.K. on Nov 2 before launching on Netflix Dec. 4.

Mulvey is renowned for both films including “Penthesilea: Queen of the Amazons” (1974) and “Riddles of the Sphinx” (1977) and pioneering essays and books, the most famous of which is “Visual Pleasure and Narrative Cinema” (1975), in which she coined the concept of the “male gaze” in cinema.

“I’ve long been interested in what happens to cinema when more kinds of people have the power to make it and have the access to watch it. How much richer our understanding of the world becomes when we experience it through different voices and perspectives,” said DuVernay. “Laura Mulvey’s work helped shift that conversation in profound ways, and I’m delighted to be the first recipient of an award in her name. Thank you to the LFCC. And here’s to the many women who will follow.”
Mulvey will present the award to DuVernay at the 47th Annual London Critics’ Circle Film Awards on Feb. 7, 2026.

“In our industry, there is a plethora of women making exceptional art, but so often budgets, awards, festival line-ups and chances are still disproportionately being awarded to their male counterparts. We are therefore delighted to have introduced this new special award, to honour and celebrate these women’s outstanding contributions,” said Jane Crowther, chair of the London Critics’ Circle Film Section. “Just like the award’s namesake Laura Mulvey,”Ava DuVernay is a true pioneer of the industry: from her exceptional filmmaking output to her extensive social impact work through ARRAY, she is a natural choice for the inaugural Female Trailblazer Award.”
